The written identity therefore overcounts by the factor N; combined with the unit-ball bounds of thm:leastsquaresbounds (tail sqrt(sum d_s^2), which itself must be bounded by CN m^{-1/q} using sigma_s^{-1} <= N s^{-1/q}) the written chain does not deliver the claimed MN-scaled rates. In (iii) the first step 'varrho_n << sup ||v - S_{c_3n} v||' also bounds a width with n points by an algorithm using c_3 n > n points, which needs a re-indexing argument that the proof omits. The theorem's stated bounds are nevertheless true once the scaling is corrected.

issues.failure_explanation: The constraint |s'|_infty <= eta in (sigma_s) acts coordinatewise, so sigma_s^2 factorizes as prod_j g_j(s_j) with g_j(k) = sum_{l<=min(k,eta)} binom(k,l) rho_j^{2l}. Along the line s = k e_1, g_1(k) <= C_eta sum_{l<=eta} k^l rho_1^{2l} <= C k^{eta} rho_1^{2eta} for k >= eta, hence sigma_{k e_1}^{-q} >= c k^{-q eta / 2}, and sum_k k^{-q eta /2} diverges whenever q*eta <= 2. Since the lq sum over FF dominates the sum along this line, ||sigma^{-1}||_{lq(FF)} = infinity whenever q*eta <= 2. Thus for eta = 1 (and any eta <= 2/q), i.e. for every q in (0,2] used by the recovery theorems, the lemma's own conclusion 'with ||sigma^{-1}||_{lq} <= N < infinity' is false. The identical conclusion is asserted in lemma:weighted summability, holomorphic with sigma given by (sigma_s) and q = p/(1-p) < 2, so it is equally false there; moreover its rho_j need not be (b,xi)-admissible since sum_j b_j rho_j = (xi/4)||b||^{p+1}/sqrt(eta!) can exceed xi, so the cited result is applied outside its hypotheses.
